studies.title: True Love Waits
studies.listen_for: Compare the space around the voice in the live guitar and studio piano settings. What changes when the accompaniment fills time differently?
studies.perspective: The two recordings offer different realizations of a recognizable song. Compare one phrase at a time, attending to accompaniment, pacing and vocal placement. Several things change together; this is a study of alternatives, not proof that one isolated production decision caused the difference.
studies.original_comparison: For Porch Light, compare a verse carried by repeated guitar attacks with one carried by overlapping piano notes. Preserve the melody and phrase lengths first, then ask which setting supports the intended delivery.

studies.title: Two Thousand and Seventeen
studies.listen_for: Keep the repeating plucked figure in mind, then follow what enters, recedes or changes around it.
studies.perspective: A recurring figure gives the ear a reference while the surrounding texture develops. Compare two separated passages and describe the audible differences before deciding whether the central idea itself has changed. Repetition can carry continuity without requiring a new melody at every turn.
studies.original_comparison: Keep Platform Three’s bass figure fixed while changing the upper entrances and instrumental density. Compare that with replacing the bass figure as well: which version makes the change easier to notice?

studies.title: Lean on Me
studies.listen_for: Follow the repeated notes, neighboring steps and larger movements in a short vocal phrase. Which distances help it remain recognizable?
studies.perspective: A familiar tune gives a useful starting point for distinguishing melodic contour from exact intervals. First describe whether a short line stays, rises or falls. Then check its actual pitch distances before using it as a model for transposition. The course does not reproduce a transcription of this recording.
studies.original_comparison: Porch Light’s E–G–A seed keeps its identity when all three notes move by the same interval. Moving individual notes by different amounts may preserve an upward contour while changing the melody’s distances.

passages.label: Opening
passages.listen_for: Listen through the opening and vocal entrance. Choose one short sung gesture and describe whether its notes stay, rise or fall before checking their distances.
